image_prompt.text: A large flat dark grey concrete floor as the main battle area, with red and blue accents marking the two team sides
Solid perimeter walls enclosing the arena on every edge, tall enough to keep fighters inside
Grey cover walls and obstacles scattered across the arena floor for tactical play, with four pillars grouped in the centre so a retreating fighter can break line of sight
Two raised platforms on opposite sides of the arena, each reached by a ramp from the floor, giving sniping and advantage positions over the fight
A raised central platform above the middle of the floor, the arena's key contested control point
Red and blue team spawn areas at opposite ends of the arena, set back and screened from the open floor

layout_placement.text: Team spawns placed out of the raised platforms' sightlines so neither side appears under fire the frame it respawns

notes: Action, not Shooter: the prompt self-declares a fighting game and the map is one shared clash space rather than firing corridors; 'sniping' describes only the two raised platforms.

Battlegrounds preset taken, but on arena-tiered instead of its arena-flat: two ramped side platforms and a raised central platform are real elevation with nothing overhanging, so the route is the tiered one rather than the preset's plain P0.
hazard-kill dropped from the preset - the prompt asks for perimeter walls around every edge, which is the opposite of ring-out edges.

Configurable attributes (arena size, wall height, platform height, number of cover walls, cover wall height) and the anchored / CanCollide requirement are build-script parameters with no layout option; the stated quantities are carried as counts on the picks.

Want that, or would you rather build it up yourself?
